jobs.title: 2026 Account Management Intern, Berlin (German Speaking) at Uber
jobs.description: Employer: Uber Expires: 09/13/2026 This internship sits at the commercial heart of Uber Eats. You'll join an Account Management team and take on real ownership of partner performance across a portfolio of restaurant brands.Account Management at Uber Eats is fundamentally a commercial function. Your job is to grow revenue for partners and for Uber. That means you'll be working with data daily, running business reviews, identifying where performance is lagging and why, and translating that analysis into concrete recommendations that move the needle.This isn't an observational role. From week one, you'll carry a workstream, supper the team with a set of accounts, and be expected to show up to conversations with a point of view grounded in data. This internship offers hands-on exposure to commercial operations, account management, customer success, and cross-functional project management in a fast-paced environment.What You’ll DoCommercial Performance & Partner GrowthSupport the AM team across a set of accounts, tracking performance against commercial KPIs: GMV, order volume, conversion rate, basket size, and customer retention.Work with the AM Team to support restaurant partners to identify growth opportunities and recommend commercial solutions.Support outbound partner conversations with clear commercial objectives.Support the sale of Ads & Offers products by articulating their value and helping partners adopt them.Run structured business reviews: prepare the analysis, identify the growth levers, and land a clear recommendation.Build the narrative behind the numbers translating data into a story that drives partner action.Support expansion conversations: new site launches, geographic growth, and cross-sell opportunities within existing accounts.Data Analysis & Insight GenerationRun structured performance diagnostics: identify where a partner is underperforming versus benchmark and why.Build and maintain reporting dashboards that surface the metrics that matter.Develop and test hypotheses about what drives partner revenue then work with the team to act on them.SQL exposure is a plus but not required; comfort with Excel or Google Sheets and a structured analytical mindset is essential.Marketing Execution & Demand GenerationExecute performance marketing campaigns promotions, visibility boosts, pricing experiments and rigorously track ROI.Identify where marketing investment will generate the highest incremental return for a given partner.Analyse post-campaign data to draw conclusions and feed learnings back into future strategy.Basic QualificationsCurrently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree program (e.g., Business Administration, Economics, Marketing, Operations, Data Analytics, or related fields), with graduation by early 2027.Available for a full-time, 6-month internship starting 7th September 2026Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets, including data extraction and analysisNative in German and fluency in EnglishStrong communication and stakeholder management skillsOpen to exploring full-time opportunities with Uber following the internship in case a role becomes available.Who Thrives HereThe interns who get the most from this role arrive curious about the numbers, comfortable being challenged on their thinking, and genuinely interested in how commercial relationships work. They take ownership early, ask sharp questions, and know the difference between being busy and having impact.If that sounds like you, we’d like to meet you~~ ~~Ready to Ride?This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we'd love to hear from you.You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.Uber is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing this form.<<<

jobs.title: Project Management Intern at Fessler & Bowman, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Fessler & Bowman, Inc. Expires: 09/14/2026 Founded in 1963 by Don Fessler & George Bowman, Fessler & Bowman, Inc. has grown from a residential flatwork & basement wall contractor to a top 100 Commercial Concrete Contractor recognized across the nation. Keeping customer satisfaction as our fundamental core value has allowed Fessler & Bowman, Inc. to prosper for nearly six decades. Our Culture & Philosophy:Fessler & Bowman is a fast-paced and culture-focused industry leader in specialty concrete and civil earthwork. When we talk about culture at F&B, it is not just a plaque hanging in our lobby. Our values are our driving force and have allowed us to build a phenomenal team delivering best in class products to our customers. Open & ConstructiveTake Pride in Our ProductRelentless CommitmentCare About Our CustomersTeam Success Summary:The Project Management Team is responsible for the successful completion of construction projects, from the initial hand-off from Estimating through final completion and close-out. PMs are responsible for overall project planning and scheduling, resource allocation, project accounting, and control, while providing technical direction and ensuring compliance with quality standards and applicable laws and regulations. As a Project Management Intern, you will assist in all of these activities by offering support and utilizing prior knowledge. The descriptions below are representative of, but not limited to, the expectations of this role. Five Key Roles of the Project Management Intern:Organizing and planning for the safe and efficient execution of the assigned projectsAssist in maintaining the financial controls of the project for the profit/loss of the projectAssisting in developing and maintaining the project scheduleCollaborating with PM team to estimate, price and negotiate the price on projectsWorking with Superintendents and Estimating teams for project collaboration Essential Duties & Responsibilities:Assisting with department initiativesContinually expanding knowledge and use of industry best practices and innovationSolving problems, as they arise, by using available knowledge and resourcesOther duties as assigned Education, Experience & Qualifications:Currently working towards a degree in Construction Management or related fieldCompetency with computers and basic programs/softwareExcellent written and oral communication skillsDetail-oriented and excellent organization skillsCreative and results-oriented, with a strong sense of urgency and self-motivationExcellent problem-solving skills, with an adaptable and flexible style in working with all types of individuals Travel:Light travel may be required for this position. Travel may include, but is not limited to, travel from office to various job sites. Fessler and Bowman will compensate for travel when applicable. Work Environment:As a Project Management Intern, you will be subject to various work environments. Environments include but are not limited to the following: office and field settings, high/low temperatures, areas close to traffic, loud and frequent noises, confined spaces, heights, indoor/outdoor settings. Recruitment Process:The recruitment process will include a phone screen, in-person meeting, and a pre-employment background check and drug test. Fessler & Bowman is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Quantitative Finance Associate Summer Internship Program 2027 New York at Barclays
jobs.description: Employer: Barclays Expires: 09/14/2026 Internship OverviewJoin us on an internship for 10 weeks within one of our Quant focused business areas. Immerse yourself in our work and culture and gain invaluable insights with this longer internship. 1-2 year targeted, fast-track program focused on developing specialist technical expertise. Why the Quant Internship Program?As an intern with Barclays, you’ll be embedded with one of our Quant teams, we’ll expect you to have a tangible impact on our business from day one, using the latest AI tools to work on algorithmic trading strategies, researching and developing models or producing data analysis tools for valuation and risk management. Applying to our program provides the opportunity to join one of our specialist teams, including: Markets Quantitative Analytics (Markets QA)Markets Quantitative Analytics develops the models, data science and insights that underpin trading, risk management and decision-making across Global Markets. By combining quantitative research, technology and market expertise, the team automates strategies, enhances analytics and delivers scalable solutions that improve franchise performance. Risk Quantitative Analytics (Risk QA)Risk Quantitative Analytics develops the models, analytics and technology that enable Barclays to measure, manage and optimise financial risk across the firm. By combining quantitative research and software engineering, the team delivers data-driven insights and scalable solutions that support decision-making, regulatory compliance and risk management. Electronic Trading (eTrading)Markets Electronic develops, operates and governs Barclays' global electronic trading capabilities, delivering the platforms, algorithms, quantitative models, client connectivity and automation that enable clients to trade seamlessly across asset classes at scale. The team combines trading, quantitative research, data science, technology, and risk control expertise to drive revenue growth, market-making, execution quality, resilience and innovation across Global Markets' eTrading franchise. The chance to make an impactFrom beginning to end, we’ll do everything in our power to make sure you get the very most from your internship, including matching you with a team that best aligns with your strengths. We’ll surround you with challenging projects and opportunities to grow and learn. We’ll keep you motivated with encouragement, feedback and support as you build your technical know-how, business acumen and leadership skills. We’ll help you connect with mentors, and network with colleagues and senior leaders alike. If you perform well, this could be the beginning of an incredible career with Barclays. Working in New YorkYou will be working at our Americas Headquarters at 745 Seventh Avenue. This 37-story office tower is located in Times Square in the heart of Manhattan and features a cafeteria, fitness center and state-of-the-art LED signage on the facade of the building. It is the policy of Barclays to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, alienage or citizenship status, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or domestic/civil partnership status, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other basis protected by law. Salary / Rate Minimum: 125,000.00Salary / Rate Maximum: 150,000.00The minimum and maximum salary/rate information above include only base salary or base hourly rate. It does not include any another type of compensation or benefits that may be available.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Summer Congressional Internship Program at Congressional Hispanic Caucus Institute (CHCI)
jobs.description: Employer: Congressional Hispanic Caucus Institute (CHCI) Expires: 09/14/2026 With CHCI’s paid internships offered during the Summer and Fall, students can apply for the program that best fits their college timeline and schedule. CHCI interns will meet accomplished leaders, including CHCI Alumni, dedicated to improving the Latino community. These leaders come from a wide range of professional backgrounds, including Capitol Hill, Fortune 500 companies, NGOs, nonprofits, and other organizations that support Latino education and leadership development. The Congressional Internship Program (CIP) equips participants with legislative knowledge, cultural competency, an extensive network, and personal and professional leadership skills. CHCI interns come to D.C. from throughout the country. They will meet fellow Latinos from different heritages and backgrounds, learning as much from each other as from CHCI. As they work together, serve the community, and explore the nation’s capital, interns will build bonds that will last beyond the program. Interns will attend weekly programming sessions centered on CHCI’s four Pillars of Leadership: Self Discovery, Transformation through Collective Power, Rooted in My Strength, and Planting Seeds for Tomorrow. The CHCI pillars provide the support needed to strategize and produce organized, culturally relevant programming with timely content to create opportunities, transform, influence, and connect the next generation of Latino leaders. APPLY NOW PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS Attend an 8-day orientation and weekly leadership development sessions throughout the program Work a minimum of 32 hours a week in congressional office assignment Participate in all CHCI-sponsored activities including Hispanic Heritage Month events, Summits, and receptions Complete community service hours Comply with CHCI policies regarding work performance and personal conduct PROGRAM BENEFITS Congressional office internship placement Great Pay: $4,776 Domestic round-trip transportation to Washington, D.C. Medical insurance during the program (all premiums paid by CHCI) Furnished housing (rent and utilities covered) Academic credit (we encourage participants to discuss this with their academic advisors) $100 per month metro stipend Weekly leadership development training Exclusive networking opportunities PROGRAM ELIGIBILITY Students must be enrolled full time and working towards their undergraduate degree in the academic period before participating. Recent graduates who graduate in the term immediately prior to the program session may apply. Applicants must be enrolled full time during Spring 2027 and/or Summer 2027 (Summer enrollment not required). Eligibility for graduates is limited to those completing their degree in the summer. High academic achievement (preference of 3.0 GPA or higher) Evidence of leadership skills and potential for leadership growth Demonstrated commitment to public service-oriented activities Superior analytical skills, outstanding oral and written communication skills If selected as a finalist, all individuals will be required to provide proof of enrollment to participate in the program Community college individuals graduating in June are eligible for the summer session if they are transferring to a 4-year institution come the Fall semester. If selected, they will be required to provide confirmation of enrollment at new institution for the Fall semester Applicants must be U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, asylees, or individuals who are lawfully authorized to work full-time without restriction for any U.S. employer and who, at the time of application, possess lawful evidence of employment authorization. International students on F-1 or M-1 visas are not eligible for CHCI programs. NOTE: Individuals who are seeking consideration under the “Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival” (DACA) policy must be eligible to work and possess valid employment authorization at the time of acceptance and must maintain continuous lawful employment authorization for the duration of the program for which the person is applying. SELECTION PROCESS The selection process is competitive, consisting of two stages: A written application An asynchronous interview. Written applications and prerecorded interviews are reviewed by a selection committee composed of program alumni, members of the CHCI Board of Directors and Advisory Council, and CHCI staff.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Designer at Moglea
jobs.description: Employer: Moglea Expires: 09/14/2026 Position: Designer 8/14/26IN-PERSON POSITION - Part - Time - 20 hours weeklyWe're seeking a part-time Designer to join our Design Team. The Design Team is responsible for various creative aspects of the Moglea brand. Applicants should have a design-focused educational background with knowledge of programs like Photoshop, InDesign, and Illustrator. Experience with video and social media is a plus. Responsibilities include but are not limited to, designing engaging email campaigns, editing images, assisting in planning and producing social media content, and shooting video footage. Our Design Team also assists our creative directors with designing new products for the Moglea line. Our Design Team also plans and coordinates marketing efforts for the brand. We’re looking for someone who is organized, flexible, and ready to bring fresh ideas to the Moglea brand.Our Company: Moglea was launched in 2012 and is under the creative direction of Chad and Meg Gleason. Their artful stationery and product line is created by using hand-applied production processes to add one-of-a-kind elements to each product. The production team in their Des Moines, Iowa-based studio thoughtfully applies layers of paint to extra-thick sheets of paper before cutting them down, yielding completely unique compositions. Each piece is finished on one of their antique presses where it is foil stamped, printed, or die-cut using traditional letterpress printing processes. The Moglea line is a joyful exploration of composition, pattern and color. For each new release, Chad and Meg intentionally focus on adding unexpected production processes or visual ideas to the current collection. The result is a product line in which each piece feels like a work of art that is meant to be shared. The Moglea line is sold worldwide, with placement in over 1000 stores. The line has been sold nationwide by retailers such as Anthropologie, West Elm, CB2, Nordstrom, and Blick Art Materials. Our ValuesSincerity: We speak honestly and from our heart. We believe in caring personally and challenging directly as a means to improve performance when working together. We share our own stories and extend space for others to share theirs. We truly think this is the best and only way we can continue to grow as a team and company. Accountability: We embrace mistakes and learn together. We listen, observe, and gather information that brings us closer to understanding our team. We take responsibility for mistakes and create solutions for how to improve. Respect: We respect and listen to all members of our team, whether new to Moglea or senior employees. We respect and value the mission of the Moglea organization and the decisions our founders make toward that vision. Empathy: We desire to truly know and understand all members of our team - their points of view, their motivations, and their personal feelings. We desire to match our team’s strengths and skills to roles that can make the most impact. Our understanding of others will help build sustainable and productive relationships that help improve the corporate intimacy within the culture at Moglea. Humility: We recognize that we can, and we will be wrong. New information, time, and new levels of understanding ask us to challenge our previously held opinions and seek to improve ourselves and our work. We will be open to feedback from our peers, those above us, and our direct reports. We will self-reflect on recent decisions and motivations. Adaptive Tenacity: We passionately commit to our goals and stick to that commitment with a spirit of open-hearted and earnest striving and life-long learning. We are growth-minded and ask that all employees continue to grow and adapt to the growth of our company. We seek to accomplish higher performance levels, improved communication, and stronger relationships with all Moglea employees. Integrity: We ask that all Moglea employees are trustworthy, do what is right, and lead by example. Ownership: We don’t wait for others to act. We take the initiative to bring about positive results. We ask that employees care about Moglea products, processes, property, and personnel just as much as an owner of the company would. Taking ownership means we are accountable for the results of our actions and that they are executed with the highest quality and in a timely manner. Joy: We acknowledge that as coworkers, we see each other more than family and friends. Work can be challenging but overall should be fun, joyful, and fulfilling to every member of the Moglea team. We seek to ensure that every employee has a net positive experience while working at Moglea. Primary duties:• Maintaining the aesthetic quality of the Moglea brand. • Designing work such as email campaigns and social media content. • Plan and execute sales and marketing campaigns. • Collect market research, identifying potential markets and testing. • Editing and preparing images for use across various platforms. • Updating shop and social media platforms with fresh content. • Shooting and editing video footage of the production team. • Assisting the Design Team with other tasks as assigned. • Planning and brainstorming new ideas for video content. • Designing brand collateral for the Moglea brand. • Developing new color palettes and mood boards for each collection. • Designing brand collateral for the Moglea Furniture line. • Developing new production processes and assisting with process execution within the studio. • Assisting with production as needed for large orders or during busy times. • Stocking and merchandising the DSM retail shop. • Assisting with events within the retail shop. • Assisting customers within the retail shop. • (potential / growth in role) - Designing products and packaging for Moglea Paper line.Desired Education/Experience/SkillsAdobe Suite, especially Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and Premier Pro. Instagram / Social media. Experience with shooting and editing video is required. Must have the ability to use basic video editing apps like CapCut, Edits and Premier Pro. Position Type: Part-time. In Person. Starting Pay Range: The pay range will be from 40-45K annual base salary with benefits. The pay range will be $ 20- $ 26 per hour for part-time positions. jobs.title: Clean Energy Intern - LIO at New York State Department of Public Service
jobs.description: Employer: New York State Department of Public Service Expires: 09/16/2026 The Clean Energy Intern will focus on the development and implementation of New York’s Climate Leadership & Community Protection Act (CLCPA) which adopts the most ambitious climate and clean energy agenda in the country. The CLCPA establishes aggressive targets to fully transition New York State to a green energy economy and provides a framework to ensure that the transition is equitable and just across all sectors. Interns will interact with senior staff at the Department of Public Service through briefings on project development and implementation.Applicants should be enrolled in a graduate program and possess the following:Desire to work in the clean energy sector, supporting renewable energy, energy efficiency, building electrification, electric vehicle charging and distributed energy resource technologiesExcellent written and verbal communication skillsStrong attention to detail and organization skillsStrong skills in generating actionable insights from data through a combination of quantitative analysis and qualitative interpretationDuties Description:The Clean Energy Intern will focus on the oversight and review activities related to the Energy Efficiency and Electric Vehicle programs based on the Climate Leadership and Communities Protection Act (CLCPA) climate goals as they pertain to LIPA compliance and efforts to reach set targets for the Long Island and Rockaways. The Department of Public Service (Department) currently oversees over $97 million in Energy Efficiency and electric vehicle programs. These programs have metrics and conducting reviews to assess performance and recommend improvements to assist with program impact, ability to meet targets, and assess market needs is crucial. The Clean Energy Intern will be a critical member of the Department Staff team overseeing this function. Activities will include, but not be limited to: Assisting senior staff assigned to the Long Island Office in fulfilling responsibilities in accordance with the Climate Leadership Community Protection Act (CLCPA) climate goals, LIPA Reform Act, specifically addressing U2.0 metrics, New Efficiency New York, Reforming the Energy Vision (REV), clean energy orders and related issues.Identifying relevant policy goals/requirements in the CLCPA as they pertain to the LIPA territory.Assisting with quarterly review of utility performance metrics and providing input on new/modified annual metrics to track.Maintaining current awareness of the Department and stakeholders’ concerns regarding Energy Efficiency (EE) programs and coordinating with the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) and the DPS Albany EE team. Assisting with external oversight and engaging in outreach activities pertinent to informing ratepayers of proposed tariff modifications, public information on consumer assistance, energy savings/efficiency programs, Long Island’s clean, renewable, and distributed energy resources, and annual Utility 2.0 and Energy Efficiency Plans\Assisting in collecting and analyzing data relevant to assessing the adequacy of existing and/or proposed metrics to determine their efficiency and effectiveness at achieving program targets and deliverables. Performing data gathering, analysis, evaluation, forecasting, and modeling for the Markets and Innovation Section of the Long Island Office. Reviewing and summarizing the public comments of Long Island residential/commercial ratepayers and assisting in developing Department responses. Reviewing and analyzing clean energy industry business practices and models both in-state and nationally. Conducting in-depth research on energy policies, regulations, and market trends to support the achievement of CLCPA targets related to renewable energy, energy efficiency, and emission reductions. Providing support on utility rate proceedings, which may include, drafting testimony; testifying; reviewing and analyzing utility energy efficiency programs and strategies, demand response programs and strategies; reviewing budgets; and analyzing and developing utility performance metrics. Providing analyses of policy implications, identifying potential challenges and opportunities for innovations. Additional Information:Salary: Graduate Interns earn $21.22/hour.Hours: Up to 37.5 hours per week. Office Location: 125 East Bethpage Road, Plainview, New YorkRemote Work: A hybrid work schedule may be possible. How to apply: Please send your resume and cover letter to recruiting@dps.ny.gov and reference “Clean Energy Internship: LIO - Fall 2026”

jobs.description: Employer: New York State Department of Public Service Expires: 09/16/2026 The Clean Energy Intern will contribute to the development and implementation of New York’s Climate Leadership & Community Protection Act (CLCPA) which adopts the most ambitious climate and clean energy agenda in the country. The CLCPA establishes aggressive targets to fully transition New York State to a green energy economy and provides a framework to ensure that the transition is equitable and just across all sectors. Interns will interact with senior staff at the Department of Public Service through briefings on project development and implementation. Applicants should be enrolled in a graduate program and possess the following:Desire to work in the clean energy sector, supporting renewable energy, energy efficiency, building electrification, electric vehicle charging and distributed energy resource technologiesExcellent written and verbal communication skillsStrong attention to detail and organization skillsStrong skills in generating actionable insights from data through a combination of quantitative analysis and qualitative interpretationDuties Description:The clean energy transition envisioned by the CLCPA will require significant changes in how buildings use energy and, in turn, how the State’s energy systems supply this energy. Data related to energy consumption patterns is critical to understand to develop viable solutions. While this data is critical, the provision of such data must include appropriate data cyber security and data privacy protections. The Clean Energy Intern will develop an in-depth knowledge of existing energy data access mechanisms and the New York Public Service Commission’s Data Access Framework. The Clean Energy Intern should comprehend risk mitigation and compliance and have an interest in the intersection between technology and the law as they apply to energy related data. Determining whether utility data related efforts and IT investments are planned and progressing at reasonable and appropriate levels to effectively meet the needs of the State policies, especially regarding time, budget, project requirements, benefit delivery, risk mitigation, and the use of industry best practices.Identifying and characterizing the types of data-related IT project implementation information required from utilities.Making recommendations regarding the requirement of communications protocols and other technical standards.Analyzing data issues to solve problems impacting data users’ respective functions.Additional Information:Salary: Graduate Interns earn $21.22/hour.Hours: Up to 37.5 hours per week. jobs.description: Employer: Fastflo Expires: 09/16/2026 Marketing Intern, B2C Growth & UGCFastflo | Remote (Cambridge, MA, hybrid welcome) | Part-time or Full-time | PaidAbout FastfloFastflo is a hyper-growth B2B SaaS startup built at the Harvard Innovation Labs. We're changing how companies hire frontline workers: instead of forcing candidates through clunky web forms, applications happen natively inside WhatsApp and iMessage. Around 80% of candidates finish their application, versus roughly 15% on traditional flows. We recently closed our seed round, and we're now launching something new: a job board built for candidates.That job board needs to be everywhere candidates are. That's your job.The RoleYou will own consumer marketing for our job board launch. Not "support" it, not "assist with" it. Own it. You'll be the person responsible for getting job seekers to discover us, and you'll have real freedom in how you do it.We do things very differently at Fastflo, and that's why we win. We're not looking for someone to schedule three polished posts a week. We're looking for someone with the creative instincts and the nerve to run guerrilla plays that bigger companies would never approve: content that gets shared, stunts that get talked about, ideas that punch far above our budget.And we're not hiring for a semester. We're hiring the person who could lead marketing at Fastflo. This internship is how you earn that: prove it and the intention is to convert you into a long-term position with real ownership of the function as we scale.What You'll DoCreate UGC yourself: short-form video for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts about job searching, careers, and our job boardBuild a machine for getting others to create UGC: creator partnerships, campus ambassadors, challenges, whatever worksRun our candidate-facing social channels and grow them from scratchInvent and execute guerrilla campaigns to drive job seekers to the boardTrack what's working and double down ruthlesslyWhat Success Looks LikeJob seekers discovering and signing up for the job board. You'll have clear growth targets, full ownership of the channels, and a direct line to the founders. When your video hits, everyone will know it was yours.Who Thrives HereCurrently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor's or master's degreeYou already make content, or you've been itching for an excuse to startA ton of initiative: you generate ideas without being asked and ship them without hand-holdingComfortable on camera, or great at getting other people to beScrappy: you see a $0 budget as a creative constraint, not an obstacleNo formal marketing experience required. Taste, energy, and output matter more.Compensation & LogisticsPaid position with performance incentives tied to growth resultsAcademic credit available where your program allows, in addition to compensationRemote by default; you're welcome to join us in person or hybrid in Cambridge if you're localPart-time or full-time depending on your availabilityThis role is designed to convert: perform well and you move into a long-term position with a path to leading marketing at Fastflo

jobs.title: Development & Communications Intern at LIFT Inc
jobs.description: Employer: LIFT Inc Expires: 09/17/2026 POSITION: Development & Communications Intern LOCATION: National REPORTS TO: Director, Individual GivingSUPERVISES: N/AFLSA STATUS: NonexemptHOURLY RATE: $22TRAVEL, TIME COMMITMENT & Duration:Local In-Person External Meetings: 0%20-25 hours per month through December 31, 2026 with the possibility of extensionABOUT OUR ORGANIZATION LIFT is on a mission to break the cycle of poverty by investing in parents. Through direct work with families, engaging technical assistance partnerships, and by advocating for policies that drive systemic change, we’re fighting poverty by lifting two generations at once. Our team culture is rooted in deep respect for the parents we partner with and for each other. We’re looking for dedicated team members who share our vision that, 25 years from now, LIFT is no longer needed because we have helped build a social service system grounded in Hope, Money, and Love, where all families can thrive. We’re guided by mission- and strategy-aligned leadership grounded in kindness, curiosity, relationships, and a commitment to equity. Explore our benefits and what it’s like to work at LIFT below –or download our Benefits & Culture Overview to learn more.*LIFT operates sites in Chicago, Los Angeles, DC, and New York. This position may be done remotely from any state where LIFT currently operates.POSITION OVERVIEW This is a part-time internship requiring approximately 20 hours per month through December 31, 2026, with the possibility of extension. This role will report to the Director, Individual Giving, and will work closely with the Communications Manager. This part-time Development & Communications intern will support LIFT’s fundraising-focused communications efforts and external-facing communications. The internship is writing-driven, with responsibility for developing donor-facing communications, social media, and organizational content, creating compelling stories and content that engage supporters, strengthen relationships, advance fundraising goals, and broaden LIFT's reach and visibility.AS THE DEVELOPMENT & COMMUNICATION INTERN YOU WILL… DevelopmentDraft and edit donor-facing communications and development content that engage supporters, communicate impact, and strengthen relationships with donors and partners. Create and refine templates and adaptable content that can be used across multiple cities, ensuring consistency while tailoring messaging for local contexts.Support the development and execution of fundraising-focused communications strategies that effectively engage and retain donors.Develop clear, concise, and compelling written content that reflects both local impact and a broader national perspective.Collaborate with internal stakeholders to gather input and ensure alignment on messaging, while working independently.Proofread and edit content with a high level of attention to detail, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and consistency in tone and branding across materials.Explore opportunities to enhance communication through visual storytelling, including basic graphic design and video content to support fundraising efforts.Support broader development and communications activities, including event preparation, coordination, and administrative support as neededCommunicationsManage LIFT's social media presence day-to-day — writing and building posts, maintaining a consistent content calendar, and adapting content across platforms.Support the writing and editing of external content including the monthly newsletter, blog posts, and the annual report.Copy edit across external materials, serving as a reliable second pair of eyes on accuracy, consistency, tone, and brand.Track relevant news, research, and field conversations to surface content opportunities.OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise, and compelling content for a range of audiences, including donors, partners, and social media audiences.Experience or interest in development and fundraising communications, donor engagement, and mission-driven storytelling.Fluency with social media as a communications tool. Comfortable writing copy and creating content for LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and Facebook, and maintaining a content calendar.Ability to work independently in a remote, flexible environment.High attention to detail, including proofreading for accuracy, consistency, and grammatical correctness.Self-motivated with a willingness to learn and grow skills in areas such as fundraising strategy, graphic design, and multimedia content (e.g., video).Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to contribute to longer-term projects by managing timelines, tracking tasks, and meeting deadlines.LIFT’S COMPETENCIESAll LIFT employees embrace and demonstrate our organization-wide core competencies:Communication: You share information with relevant parties in a clear and timely manner; effectively engage with and present to others; and write and verbally communicate in a manner that conveys understanding of relevant information and issues.Accountability: You take responsibility for the quality and timeliness of work and achieve results with appropriate levels of oversight. You receive feedback in a constructive manner.Inclusiveness: You help create a work environment that appreciates diversity and encourages equity by treating others with respect, listening to, and demonstrating appreciation for others’ perspectives, and using culturally sensitive language.Teamwork: You work effectively with others throughout the organization and promote cooperation and commitment within your team to achieve goals and deliverables.Results-orientation: You focus on results and desired outcomes, keeping team and organizational goals in mind. You use sound planning to achieve goals and get the job done.Problem-solving: You take the initiative to solve problems. You exhibit resourcefulness, innovation, and adaptability to new situations.Don’t think you have everything for this role but are still interested? Please don’t hesitate to apply. We’d love to hear from you! LIFT is an equal opportunity employer and believes that diversity in all dimensions of the organization supports and bolsters the innovative thinking essential to its success and is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants. LIFT’s goal is for our people to reflect the communities in which we live and serve and to ensure representation of people of color, those who identify as women, veterans, and individuals with disabilities in our organization. WHAT WE OFFER Hourly rate: $22/hour. LIFT’s compensation philosophy is to pay competitively for our non-profit sector and ensure equity across the organization. The compensation range we offer represents a good faith estimate of what we may pay for the position at the time of posting. To ensure we meet our equity and inclusion standards, where a candidate is placed in the range will be assessed based on the market for the position, their qualifications, internal equity, and budget. We will discuss where you are likely to fall within the posted range during the recruitment process, and LIFT will present our best salary offer first.

jobs.description: Employer: Target - Stores Expires: 09/18/2026 ALL ABOUT TARGETAs a Fortune 50 company with more than 400,000 team members worldwide, Target is an iconic brand and one of America's leading retailers.Working at Target means the opportunity to help all families discover the joy of everyday life. Caring for our communities is woven into who we are, and we invest in the places we collectively live, work, and play. We prioritize relationships, fuel and develop talent by creating growth opportunities, and succeed as one Target team. At our core, our purpose is ingrained in who we are, what we value, and how we work. It’s how we care, grow, and win together.ALL ABOUT THE STORES EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP INTERNSHIPExperience firsthand what it’s like to lead a retail team within a Target store. This internship is a paid 40 hr/week, hands-on training program to develop and prepare for your store leadership. As a Stores Executive Intern, you will get a valuable realistic preview of the Executive Team Leader role (Assistant Store Manager) over a defined period of time. Within this store management internship, you will work closely with other managers and team members to develop an understanding of how Target’s retail business works and what it takes to excel in a management role. You will be introduced to multiple areas of the store’s business, but the majority of your time will be spent leading amongst the team, identifying and working towards store priorities, and delivering great guest service. The goal of the Stores Executive internship is to provide a realistic job preview of an ETL role. jobs.description: Employer: Guidewell Expires: 09/18/2026 Enterprise Analytics Summer 2027 Internship Are you a current college student who's curious about how data can improve healthcare? This is a paid, 11-week summer internship on one of our analytics teams — designed for students who are still completing their degree and want real-world experience before heading back to school in the fall. Duration: 11 weeks, starting in May 2027 Location: Jacksonville, FL (in-person) Our GuideWell campus in Jacksonville, FL features renovated office buildings surrounding a beautiful pond and walking path. The campus is highlighted by an athletic complex, fitness center, as well as a full-service cafeteria and a coffee shop. Other features include intramural sports, an open office environment, and employee activities. All of this within a culture that embraces flexibility, innovation, and diversity. Bring your unique talents and perspective to help us make a difference! What to Expect You'll work in person on our Jacksonville, FL campus alongside a cohort of fellow summer interns and full-time analysts. Over the course of the summer, you'll contribute to a meaningful project with real business impact — building technical skills, learning how healthcare analytics works, and presenting your findings to the team. What the Summer Includes A real analytics project with healthcare data that you'll complete with the support of a dedicated manager Housing provided to those not local to Jacksonville Team-building activities with other interns and staff Exposure to multiple areas and people across our analytics organizations Access to campus amenities (fitness center, cafeteria, walking paths, intramural sports, and more) The Kind of Work You'll Do Past interns have built interactive visualization tools, analyzed member health trends to surface actionable insights, and conducted research that informed business strategy — all using real data in a supportive, collaborative environment. Who Tends to Thrive Here Curious and eager to learn, even in unfamiliar territory Genuinely interested in healthcare as a space to make a difference Comfortable working in person and collaborating with a team Excited to get hands-on with data, even if still building technical skills Minimum Requirements Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program (not graduating before August 2027) Coursework and/or personal projects that demonstrate a quantitative mindset Exposure to analytical tools or writing code for data manipulation and visualization (e.g., SQL, R, etc.)Strong written and verbal communication skills Must have and maintain a 3.0 cumulative grade point average (GPA) or better at the time of application, throughout the application process, and for the duration of the internship program. Other Details This team does not use tools to automatically review cover letters and resumes. Genuine cover letters in your own words are strongly preferred — we value your voice over a polished template. Further, please only submit thoughtfully considered applications that reflect your actual experiences and interests. Members of our team look forward to reviewing them. What We Offer: As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living.To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance; Income protection benefits: life insurance, Short- and long-term disability programs; Leave programs to support personal circumstances; Retirement Savings Plan includes employer contribution and employer match; Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 corporate holidays and 2 well-being days Additional voluntary benefits available; and A comprehensive wellness program Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ. To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. Typical Hourly Pay Range: $24 - $26 We are an Equal Opportunity/Protected Veteran/Disabled Employer committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and equitable culture for our employees and communities.

jobs.title: Pro Bono Innovations Fund Intern - Fall 2026 at Legal Services Corporation
jobs.description: Employer: Legal Services Corporation Expires: 09/18/2026 Position: Pro Bono Innovations Fund Intern Location: Washington, DC 20006Department: Office of Program Performance (OPP)Employment Status: Part-Time| Non-exempt | Hybrid | DC-Metro Area Only OVERVIEW:Established by Congress in 1974, the Legal Services Corporation (LSC) is the country’s single largest funder of civil legal aid for low-income Americans. LSC currently funds 129 independent legal aid offices nationwide. LSC’s mission is to promote equal access to justice and provide grants for high-quality civil legal assistance to low-income Americans.The Office of Program Performance (OPP) oversees LSC’s grantmaking and works with grantees to support high-quality legal services and effective program performance. Within OPP, the Pro Bono Innovation Fund (PBIF) supports innovative and effective approaches to expanding pro bono legal services. PBIF’s work includes grant administration, grantee support and technical assistance, program evaluation, research, and initiatives designed to strengthen and improve pro bono service delivery.The internships are based in Washington, DC, and will require working from an office in DC in accordance with LSC’s hybrid work model. The successful candidates must live in the DC metropolitan area for the duration of the internship. BASIC FUNCTION:The primary objectives of this internship are for the intern to:Develop a practical understanding of grantmaking, grant administration, program evaluation, and technical assistance within civil legal aid;Strengthen research, data analysis, professional writing, and presentation skills through substantive PBIF projects;Build experience reviewing grant applications, progress reports, supporting materials, and program data to identify trends, successes, challenges, and lessons learned;Strengthen project management, time management, professional communication, and effective workplace behaviors while supporting multiple projects;Gain hands-on experience using PBIF’s grant management, data tracking, and collaboration tools and processes.The internship is expected to run from September through December 2026. Interns will work part-time, up to 20 hours per week during the fall. PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:The intern's principal duties and responsibilities include:Supporting PBIF grant administration and reporting activities, including preparing progress report and payment request materials, reviewing reports for completeness, compiling data, and helping track reporting requirements and deadlines.Assisting with grantee communications and progress report preparation by reviewing grant applications, reports, and supporting materials; preparing materials for calls; tracking follow-up items; and participating in grantee meetings as appropriate.Conducting research and analysis related to PBIF grants, including reviewing past Sustainability grants and other grantee data to identify program successes, challenges, lessons learned, and opportunities for improvement.Supporting PBIF program evaluation activities by organizing and preparing information for external evaluators, assisting with data collection and analysis, and supporting related communications and data transfers.Assisting with the development of curriculum, workshops, presentations, visualizations, internal reference tools, and other resources for PBIF initiatives, including the PBIF Incubation grantee class and PBIF Grantee Meeting.Supporting planning and preparation for PBIF meetings, trainings, and events, including researching topics, organizing materials, assisting with logistics, and preparing supporting resources.Reviewing, organizing, and updating grant-related data and records using systems such as GrantEase, Smartsheet, Microsoft Excel, and other OPP tools.Drafting and editing templates, checklists, correspondence, presentations, reports, and other materials that support PBIF grant administration and program improvement.Participating in PBIF team and stakeholder meetings, taking notes, tracking action items, and coordinating follow-up activities with PBIF staff.Assisting with other OPP and PBIF projects and duties as assigned. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:We are accepting applications from current undergraduate, graduate, and law students, as well as recent graduates of post-secondary institutions.The ideal applicant must be:Organized and attentive to detail;Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint;Strong in research, data analysis, written communication, and verbal communication;Comfortable reviewing detailed information, organizing data, and managing multiple assignments and deadlines;Able to work independently and collaboratively, ask thoughtful questions, and communicate professionally with team members and stakeholders;Intellectually curious and interested in learning about grantmaking, program evaluation, technical assistance, and civil legal aid;Committed to LSC’s mission of promoting equal access to justice;Interest or background in law, public policy, nonprofit management, program evaluation, research, data analysis, grants administration, or related fields preferred;Bonus: Experience with Smartsheet, data visualization, data management, presentation development, or grant management systems. HOURLY RATE:This position pays $20 to $22 per hour, based on your education level and internship status. APPLICATION PROCESS:To apply, visit www.lsc.gov/about-lsc/careers. Please submit:A current résuméA cover letter explaining your interest in this internship and how your goals align with LSC’s mission Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. If you need accommodations during the application process, email jobapplicant@lsc.gov.LSC is an equal-opportunity employer.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Grant Writer Intern at Social Responsibility Through Me
jobs.description: Employer: Social Responsibility Through Me Expires: 09/18/2026 SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY THROUGH MEsrtme.org | Camden, NJ | info@srtmworks.orgPOSITION OPENSeptember 2026Grant Writer InternPaid Internship | Part-Time, Flexible | Remote-Friendly | September 2026 – May 2027 Position at a GlanceOrganizationSocial Responsibility Through Me (SRTM)Position TitleGrant Writer InternInternship PeriodSeptember 2026 – May 2027 (9 months)Hours Per Week15 hours/week — flexible scheduleLocationRemote work available; occasional in-person in Camden, NJ preferredStipend$3,000 for the full internship period (September–May)Performance Bonus$500 bonus available upon achievement of grant goalEligibilityCurrently enrolled college students (sophomore, junior, or senior preferred)Reports ToCEO / Development Director, Shaneka M. Boucher About Social Responsibility Through MeSocial Responsibility Through Me (SRTM) is a Camden, New Jersey nonprofit organization founded in 2010 with a mission to engage, employ, and empower youth and adults in underserved communities. Through afterschool enrichment programs, workforce development, and community partnerships, SRTM creates pathways to economic mobility for the families we serve. Our programs currently support over 700 youth and adults. iWe operate multiple afterschool sites across Camden City and County, and are in an active growth phase with a $1.6 million operating budget and a $315,000 fundraising goal for 2026–2027. This internship is a genuine opportunity to contribute to work that directly changes lives — and to build real, résumé-ready grant writing experience in the process. The OpportunitySRTM is seeking a motivated, detail-oriented college student to join our development team as a Grant Writer Intern for the 2026–2027 academic year. This is not a filing or data-entry internship. You will be doing real grant writing — researching funders, drafting narrative proposals, compiling application materials, and submitting grants on behalf of an organization whose work you will come to know deeply. By the end of this internship, you will have submitted a minimum of 5 grant applications to real funders, built a portfolio of professional writing samples, developed a working knowledge of the NJ philanthropic landscape, and gained hands-on experience in nonprofit development that most students don't access until their first professional job. Compensation & Bonus Structure BASE STIPEND$3,000Paid over the full internship period (September 2026 – May 2027). Disbursed in monthly installments of approximately $333/month.PERFORMANCE BONUS$500Awarded at the end of the internship period if the intern successfully submits all 5 assigned grant applications by their deadlines, with all required components complete and meeting SRTM's quality standard. Total PotentialA Grant Writer Intern who meets all goals can earn $3,500 total over the 9-month internship — $3,000 base stipend + $500 performance bonus. Payment terms: the base stipend will be issued as 1099 compensation. Interns are responsible for their own taxes. SRTM will issue the $500 bonus upon verification that all 5 applications were submitted on time and meet quality standards as determined by the CEO. Core ResponsibilitiesThe Grant Writer Intern is responsible for the following activities across the internship period: GRANT RESEARCH & CALENDAR MANAGEMENTResearch and identify grant opportunities aligned with SRTM's mission in youth development, workforce development, afterschool programming, and economic mobility.Verify funder eligibility requirements — geographic focus, organizational eligibility, program alignment, and award range — before recommending any grant for pursuit.Maintain SRTM's Grant Calendar tab: update deadlines, application status, assigned amounts, and notes for all grants in the pipeline.Provide the CEO with a bi-weekly pipeline update identifying grants due in the next 60 days and any action items requiring CEO input. GRANT WRITING & APPLICATION PREPARATIONDraft full grant narratives for a minimum of 5 grant applications across the internship period, working from SRTM's program data, impact reports, and the Fundraising SOP framework.Write clearly and compellingly for nonprofit funders — leading with outcomes and data, not activities; using Camden-specific community need data to contextualize SRTM's work.Compile all required application attachments: IRS determination letter, 990, board list, audited financials, organizational budget, and program one-pagers — from SRTM's Grant Ready Folder.Ensure all applications are submitted a minimum of 72 hours before the funder's deadline. No exceptions.Submit all applications through the funder's required portal or method, save confirmation receipts, and update the Grant Tracker the same day as submission. GRANT TRACKING & REPORTING SUPPORTUpdate SRTM's Grant Tracker within 24 hours of any grant activity — application submitted, funder contact made, award or decline received.Support the Development Director in preparing interim and final grant reports for active grants as assigned.Help compile program outcome data from SRTM's five dashboard trackers (Attendance, Behavior, Homework, Voucher, Manager) for use in grant applications and reports.Assist with writing thank-you letters and acknowledgments to funders upon grant awards. LEARNING & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENTParticipate in weekly check-in meetings with the CEO/Development Director (30 minutes, remote or in-person).Attend at least one NJ nonprofit or funder information session during the internship period (virtual attendance acceptable).Review and apply SRTM's Fundraising Standard Operating Procedures as the guide for all development activities.Provide written feedback at the midpoint and end of the internship on the experience, challenges, and suggestions for improvement. The 5-Grant Goal — What Success Looks LikeThe intern is responsible for submitting 5 complete, quality grant applications between September 2026 and May 2027. These will be selected collaboratively with the CEO from SRTM's Grant Calendar based on the intern's start date, funder deadlines, and available program data. Below is a sample of what the 5-grant portfolio might look like: #Funder (Sample)Ask AmountTarget DeadlineCategory1Turrell Fund (NJ)$15,000–$25,000Sept/Oct 2026Youth Development / Afterschool2Campbell Soup Foundation$10,000–$20,000Jan 2027Education / Community (Camden)3Claneil Foundation$5,000–$15,000Feb 2027General Operating / Youth4TD Charitable Foundation$10,000–$20,000Rolling 2027Education / Workforce5NJ DOE After3 or similar$20,000–$50,000Spring 2027Afterschool / Academic Support Final grant selections will be confirmed during the intern's first week based on actual funder deadlines, current Grant Calendar status, and SRTM's program data availability. The intern will not be expected to submit grants for which SRTM does not have the necessary supporting documentation. What We Are Looking For Required QualificationsCurrently enrolled as a college sophomore, junior, or senior (or recent graduate within 6 months of graduation)Strong written communication skills — ability to write clearly, concisely, and compellingly for a professional audienceDetail-oriented and highly organized — grant writing is unforgiving of errors and missed deadlinesSelf-directed and able to work independently with minimal supervision in a remote environmentComfortable with Google Workspace or Microsoft Office (Docs/Word, Sheets/Excel)Genuine interest in nonprofit work, social justice, youth development, or community economic developmentPreferred QualificationsCoursework or experience in nonprofit management, public policy, social work, communications, English, education, or a related fieldPrevious writing experience — journalism, academic research, persuasive writing, communications internship, or similarFamiliarity with grant writing or fundraising concepts (even from a class or volunteer experience)Knowledge of Camden, NJ or experience working in under-resourced communitiesAbility to visit SRTM's Camden site at least once during the internship period What You Will GainThis internship is designed to give you real professional experience — not make-work tasks. Here is what you will leave with: Portfolio of Real Work5 submitted grant applications to real funders — professional writing samples you can use in job applications and interviews immediately.Sector KnowledgeA working understanding of the NJ philanthropic landscape, including how community foundations, corporate foundations, and government funders make decisions.Nonprofit Operations ExperienceExposure to a real nonprofit's development systems, program data, and funding strategy — the behind-the-scenes work most students don't see until their first job.Professional MentorshipWeekly direct access to SRTM's CEO, who has 15+ years of experience in nonprofit leadership and community development in South Jersey.Letters of RecommendationStrong performers will receive a detailed, personalized letter of recommendation from the CEO upon completion of the internship.Professional NetworkConnections to SRTM's partner organizations, employer partners, and NJ nonprofit community — a network that takes most people years to build.Schedule, Location & Logistics Hours15 hours per week. The intern and supervisor will agree on a schedule during the first week. Hours are flexible and can be arranged around class schedules.Remote WorkThe majority of work can be completed remotely. Interns are expected to attend weekly virtual check-in meetings and may be asked to visit SRTM's Camden office occasionally for orientation, events, or collaborative sessions.Internship PeriodSeptember 2026 – May 2027. The intern is expected to complete the full internship period to receive the full stipend. Interns who leave before May 2027 will receive a prorated stipend based on months completed. The $500 bonus requires full completion.ToolsSRTM uses Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive). All grant tracking, research, and writing will be conducted in shared Google documents. A personal laptop or computer with internet access is required.Academic CreditSRTM is happy to support academic internship credit requirements. The CEO will complete any required supervisor evaluations or forms needed by your institution. How to ApplySRTM welcomes applications from college students of all backgrounds, especially those with personal connections to Camden or communities like it. You do not need prior grant writing experience to apply — you need strong writing skills, curiosity, and the drive to do the work. #SubmitDetails1RésuméCurrent résumé — one page preferred. Include all relevant coursework, writing experience, volunteer work, or extracurriculars.2Writing SampleOne writing sample of your choice — ideally something persuasive, research-based, or analytical. Academic papers are fine. If you have any nonprofit or grant writing samples, include those.3Short Cover LetterNo more than one page. Tell us: why SRTM's mission connects with you, what writing experience you bring (any kind), and what you hope to learn from this internship. Be specific — generic cover letters are immediately apparent.4OptionalIf you have completed any grant writing courses, workshops, or have access to a sample grant application you have written, include it as a bonus attachment. Send Applications ToNicquera Allen: msnallen@srtme.orgApplication DeadlineRolling — applications reviewed as received. Priority consideration given to applications submitted by August 15, 2026. Internship begins September 2026.Questions?Reach out to Ms. Nicquera Allen directly at msnallen@srtme.org or 856-952-2574. SRTM is a small team and we respond to every inquiry personally. Equal Opportunity StatementSocial Responsibility Through Me is an equal opportunity organization. We actively welcome applications from students of color, first-generation college students, students from Camden and South Jersey, students with disabilities, and students who bring lived experience in the communities we serve. We believe the best grant writers for SRTM are those who understand our community from the inside.SRTM does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.description: Employer: Kendall County Expires: 09/18/2026 Administration Graduate School InternType:InternSalary/Pay Rate:$20.00 Per hourPosted Date:08/05/2026Position SummaryThis internship provides graduate-level professional work experience within Kendall County’s Administration Department. Under the supervision of the County Administrator, the GraduateSchool Intern conducts independent research and analysis to support Kendall County’s operations and strategic initiatives. The role offers practical exposure to local governmentadministration, including, but not limited to policy development, grant writing, benchmarking, budgeting, communications, and organizational improvement projects. This graduate levelinternship may be paid or unpaid and eligible for school credit (at the discretion of the County Administrator). Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesThe essential duties for this internship include, but are not limited to the following: Applies graduate-level education to complex organizational issues including, but not limited to policy development, budget analysis and projections, benchmarking studies, development and implementation of strategic initiatives, operational assessments, communications, and organizational improvement projects.Independently researches complex policy, financial, operational, and legislative issues; prepares written analyses; and presents recommendations for consideration by the County Administrator and other County leadership.Assists with grant research, grant writing, grant administration, and post-award compliance reporting.Coordinates and manages assigned projects from initiation through completion, including gathering data, communicating with departments, monitoring project milestones, and preparing status updates.Evaluates administrative processes and recommends improvements to records management, operational procedures, and workflow efficiencies while ensuring compliance with applicable laws and record retention requirements.Drafts correspondence, reports, Board memoranda, grant applications, policies, ordinances, resolutions, presentations, communications, recommendations, and other professional documents requiring independent judgment and analysis.Attends Kendall County Board and Committee meetings as requested, both during and after business hours.Handles confidential matters daily relating to all functions of the Administration and maintains confidentiality of such information.Collaborates with County departments, elected officials, employees, outside agencies, consultants, and community stakeholders to gather information, coordinate projects, and facilitate implementation of County initiatives.Complies with all applicable laws, regulations, union contracts, and County policies and procedures regarding or relating to assigned job duties.Performs other duties as assigned. QualificationsTo perform this internship successfully, an individual must be able to perform all essential duties and responsibilities satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of theknowledge, skill, and/or ability required for the internship: Language Skills:1. Demonstrated ability to conduct research, synthesize complex information, prepare professional reports, and communicate recommendations clearly both orally and in writing.2. Requires proficient knowledge of the English language, spelling and grammar and ability to alphabetize.Mathematical Skills:1. Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.2. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.3. Ability to analyze financial information, budgets, statistical data, operational metrics, and performance measurements using spreadsheet software and other analytical tools.Reasoning Ability:1. Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form.2. Ability to evaluate complex issues, analyze alternatives, exercise sound judgment, identify practical solutions, and make recommendations with minimal supervision.Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations:Current and valid driver’s license.Other Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:1. Strong organization and multi-tasking skills.2. Excellent prioritization skills and the ability to meet deadlines.3. The ability to display a positive, cooperative, professional, and team orientated attitude.4. The ability to listen, understand information and ideas, and work effectively with County personnel, department heads, and elected officials.5. Ability to work with minimal supervision while exercising independent judgment.6. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills.7. Excellent research abilities.8. Ability to interpret laws, regulations, policies, financial information, and governmental procedures.9. Must be proficient in the use of computers and in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Teams, and PowerPoint.10. Must be proficient in the use of Microsoft Excel for financial forecasting and data analysis.11. Knowledge of office practices, principles of modern record keeping, and maintaining filing systems.12. Skilled in operating a personal computer, facsimile machine, copier, and typewriter.Education and Experience:Currently enrolled in, or recently graduated (within three months), from an accredited graduate degree program in Public Administration, Public Policy, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Political Science, Urban Planning, Economics, Human Resources, Organizational Leadership, or another graduate program relevant to local government administration. Physical DemandsWhile performing the duties of this internship, the intern must be able to:Frequently sit for long periods of time at a desk or in meetings.Frequently work with computers and look at computer screen and other electronic devices.Occasionally lift and/or move up to 40 pounds.Frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.Use hands to finger, handle, feel, grip, and type.Reach, push, and pull with hands and arms.Talk and hear in person and via use of telephone.Specific vision abilities include close and distance vision, as well as depth perception.Travel independently to other County properties to perform assigned internship responsibilities. Work EnvironmentThe work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an intern encounters during this internship. While performing the duties of this internship, an intern maybe subject to the following working conditions:Mostly inside environmental conditions, except when outside traveling between various buildings/locations in Kendall County to perform assigned duties.The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet to moderately quiet.The intern may be exposed to stressful and difficult situations and material.The intern may be required to provide their own transportation to travel to and from the internship site location and other County properties.Apply Here

FTI Consulting is looking to invest in your future and the future of FTI Consulting with our summer 2027 internship program, which takes place between late May 2027 and August 2027. The internship program at FTI Consulting serves as a key pathway to entry-level consultant positions, providing interns with the opportunity to gain valuable experience and be considered for future full-time roles. Technology Intern Our technology interns work with corporations, governments and law firms to meet critical legal and regulatory needs, including investigations, e-discovery, information governance, digital forensics, data privacy, document review consulting as well as project management. Consultants will start by learning a range of skills around data including e-discovery, digital forensics and case management. Advanced Analytics Researcher Intern Our advanced analytics researcher interns work closely with corporate clients and law firms to play a critical role within our Find Facts Fast (FFF) service, conducting investigative fact-finding with advanced analytics to mine large datasets and perform substantive research and analysis to quickly identify case-critical documents and prepare comprehensive summaries and documentation of the material facts, key issues and themes for strategic decision-making. Advanced Analytics Researchers will learn and develop a range of skills in FTI’s Find Facts Fast and advanced analytics research, and also around e-discovery and document review consulting. What You’ll Do As an Intern, you will become a member of a project team and work closely with our professionals and senior leaders to meet our clients’ needs. We strongly recommend you take time to educate yourself on the Technology segment, one of our five business segments, as well as the practice areas within Technology on our Careers Site. While submitting your application, you will have the opportunity to select your practice area and location based on your interests. The available practices and market locations for this segment are listed below: Technology (TECH)Location(s): Atlanta, GA; Chicago, IL; Houston, TX; Los Angeles, CA; New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Washington, DCAdvanced AnalyticsLocation(s): Chicago, IL; Los Angeles, CA; New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Washington, DCHow You’ll Grow We are committed to investing and supporting you in your professional development, and we have developed a range of programs focused on fostering leadership, growth and development opportunities. You’ll be assigned a dedicated coach to mentor, guide and support you through regular coaching sessions and serve as an advocate for your professional growth. As you progress through your career at FTI Consulting, we offer tailored programs for critical professional milestones to ensure you are prepared and empowered to take on your next role. What You Will Need To Succeed Basic Qualifications Actively pursuing a full-time bachelor’s degree or completing a fifth-year master’s program with a graduation date between December 2027 – September 2028.
