jobs.title: Institutional Growth & AI Outreach Intern at Watermark Donut Company
jobs.description: Employer: Watermark Donut Company Expires: 09/19/2026 Job Title: Institutional Growth & AI Outreach Intern for Boston’s premier Dunkin’ Franchise.Role: Develop a proprietary institutional catering business, focusing on businesses, hospitals and schools in our footprint.Company: Watermark Donut Company, LLC- 22 Boston Locations plus 2 Cambridge and 1 Charlestown.Corporate Office: 100 Grossman Drive Suite 307 Braintree, MA 02184; accessible via Red line.Time Commitment: Part-Time (15-20 hours/week) | Flexible around class schedulesCompensation: Competitive Hourly Base + Performance-Based Commission KickerAbout UsWatermark Donut Company, LLC runs a high-volume portfolio of 25 Dunkin’ locations strategically clustered throughout Downtown Boston, the Seaport, Cambridge, Charlestown and major medical hubs (MGH, Tufts, Longwood Medical, and Boston Medical Center). We are launching an innovative, tech-forward push to develop a B2B Catering Business. We are looking for a sharp, autonomous student to help us build our direct sales pipeline.The RoleThis is not a "coffee delivery" internship. You will be working directly with our leadership as well as Dunkin’s corporate team to build a modern B2B sales engine from scratch. Your mission is to develop a network of institutional catering customers in areas proximate to our stores. You will leverage cutting-edge AI prospecting tools to identify, message, and close corporate partnerships with tech firms, professional offices, pharma reps, educational institutions, and hospital floor managers.Key ResponsibilitiesAI-Powered Prospecting: Utilize generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude) and sales databases to automate and personalize hyper-local B2B outreach. Objective is to identify key contacts and then deploy smart "bounce-back" campaigns to add corporate customers to our platform.Targeted Local Networking: Coordinate with ezCater to facilitate deliveries. Develop an AI-driven email outreach program targeting potential catering customers in areas proximate to our stores.Account Optimization: Ensure our menu interfaces are optimized for corporate “Bundles" and bulk-order options.What We Are Looking ForThe Hustle: A current student (BU, BC, Northeastern, Suffolk, or similar) studying Business, Hospitality, Tech, or Entrepreneurship.Tech Fluency: You already use AI tools to accelerate your workflow and know how to prompt effectively for professional copywriting and data sorting.Local Navigation: You know the layout of our markets.Autonomy: You love a role where you aren't micro-managed. You view the hundreds of potential catering customers near our stores as a portfolio of opportunities to mine.What's In It For You?Real-World AI & B2B Experience: Build a real sales funnel on your resume using modern tech tools.Flexible Hours: We will completely work around your class schedule.Financial Upside: A solid hourly base rate protects your time, but a commission kicker on new account revenue means your earning potential is directly tied to growth in catering.Physical Demands and Working ConditionsWork is primarily performed in a professional office environment, with periodic local travel to Watermark Donut Company store locations, prospective customer sites, meetings, and other business locations throughout the Greater Boston area. Travel may involve driving, walking, or public transportation. The position requires prolonged computer and telephone use, as well as occasional standing, walking, bending, reaching, climbing stairs, and carrying business-related materials weighing up to approximately 25 pounds. Store and customer visits may involve exposure to varying weather conditions and typical retail and food-service environments.Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) StatementWatermark Donut Company, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.This job description does not constitute a contract of employment. Employment with Watermark Donut Company, LLC is at-will and may be terminated by either party at any time, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law.

We want to see your eye, your editing style, and your energy. Email everything to: marisa@washnaturals.com

jobs.title: Media and Marketing Intern at Seneca Hills Bible Camp
jobs.description: Employer: Seneca Hills Bible Camp Expires: 09/19/2026 Seneca Hills Media & Marketing InternshipAre you someone with a gifts in media arts who wants to make a difference this summer? Can you see yourself leading a team of others, capturing and editing games, rock climbing, high-energy services, nature hikes, and more. We're looking for some to create excellent content to share what God is doing at camp. Major Goal:To advance the purpose of Seneca Hills, this intern will serve in a leadership role in the areas of camp media with Christian ethics and integrity. The Media Intern will meet weekly with a member of the Executive Staff to set and discuss goals and experiences to challenge themselves through their time with Seneca Hills.Our Goals1. Encourage students or recent graduates to explore their gifts, potential career interests, and God's call in their lives.2. Provide a setting with a steady stream of fresh ideas, enthusiasm, accountability, and guidance.3. Allow interns to observe the fundamentals of good leadership and healthy public communication.4. Provide a safe place for interns to develop and try new strategies that move our vision forward.5. Allow students to gain an understanding of how a non-profit operates.6. Provide interns with an opportunity to develop professional behavior.7. Allow the student to gain practical insight and understanding into a variety of camp and business operations.Values• We believe that students can and should have a strategic role in the ministry.• We believe that serving others is a high calling.• We believe in the integration of faith and work• We believe that we should pursue excellence in all we do.Duties & ResponsibilitiesTraining• Work with the Program Director to develop a Staff Training Week In-Service schedule that will prepare new Media staff for their duties, including:• Care of equipment• Basic photography/videography skills• Basic video editing skills• Basic SongShow Plus skills• Basic Adobe Lightroom skills• How to use Vimeo, and other Social Media Sites online photo hosting interface• Throughout the summer, assist Media staff in developing skills in the areas they desire to learn and in areas where you note that learning is necessary for adequate job performance.Daily Scheduling and Responsibilities• Get copies of the weekly program schedule from the Program Director on Sunday in order to be prepared for the events of the week.• Develop a schedule of daily duties to ensure that all necessary work is completed by the Media Department. (see Media Staff Job Description for a list of Media Department duties).• Develop a “shot checklist” and delegate to the Media Staff ensure that all necessary photos are taken during a given week.• Arrange the schedule such that the Media Staff work in their areas of strength and interest. If a Media Staff member desires to work outside their area of strength, make time to work alongside them and help them to develop their skills.• Touch base with GLS about personal laptops, network needs, and A/V needs for the week on Sunday afternoon.Video & Photographs• Capture video footage and photographs of the campers and camp activities throughout each week containing group shots of camp activities, clear faces, and clips from the chapel, • bible study, and missions.• Ensure that a cabin photo is taken for every cabin and that every camper appears in a photo at least once in a clear close-up manner.• Transfer video footage and photos to the computer at least twice daily, and edit video when possible.• Where appropriate, edit photos using Adobe Lightroom.• Post current pictures on camp website daily for purchase by parents of campers.• Interview Guest Leadership for the video by Friday morning.• Edit, finalize, and upload to Vimeo by Friday nightAudio/Video Support for Chapel / Missions / Bible Study• Run the song selection program for worship.• Run power point and soundboard for the chapel, bible study, and missions.• Arrive at the chapel with worship team for setting up mics and songs for practice (usually 30-60 minutes before the start of the chapel).

jobs.title: Communications & Media (BMG) Intern - Fall 2026 at OneHope
jobs.description: Employer: OneHope Expires: 09/19/2026 OneHope is a global ministry that seeks to catalyze a movement to help every child in every generation encounter Jesus through engagement with God's Word. By working with local churches, international ministry partners, schools, and governments, we have been able to reach over 2 billion children with a relevant Gospel message since we began in 1987. Our internship program, Cultivate, is located in our international headquarters in South Florida. This program was born out of OneHope’s 30+ years of experience in research, program design, and outcome-based ministry. We are a large, innovative nonprofit that seeks to match your God-given gifts with a God-driven mission. The goal is to equip college students and recent graduates to work in a faith-based, international organization through mentorship by experienced practitioners and by providing significant opportunities for personal, spiritual, and professional growth.We are looking for a creative and highly motivated Communications & Media (BMG) Intern to support the Bible Media Group team. This role is ideal for someone passionate about social media, storytelling, content creation, and visual communication. As part of this position, you will help manage social media platforms, develop engaging content, and assist with photo and video projects that communicate BMG's work and impact. You will have opportunities to develop your creative skills while gaining hands-on experience in communications within a collaborative, mission-driven environment. Key Responsibilities:Assist with the day-to-day management of BMG's social media platformsCreate engaging social media content, including graphics, captions, photos, short-form videos, and other digital assetsHelp plan and maintain a consistent social media content calendarAssist with filming, editing, and producing video content for social media and other communication needsSupport storytelling efforts by identifying and developing stories that highlight BMG's work and impactCollaborate with the team to brainstorm creative ideas and campaignsEnsure content follows established brand guidelines and maintains a consistent voice and visual identityMonitor content performance and engagement to help identify opportunities for improvementOrganize and maintain digital media assets, including photos, videos, graphics, and other contentProvide additional communications support as needed What We’re Looking For:Strong alignment with OneHope's mission, vision, and valuesInterest or experience in communications, marketing, social media, digital media, or a related fieldStrong creative instincts and an eye for engaging visual contentFamiliarity with social media platforms and current digital content trendsExperience with Canva or similar graphic design toolsBasic video editing skills or a willingness to learnStrong written and verbal communication skillsSelf-motivated, organized, and able to manage multiple projects and deadlinesDetail-oriented with a willingness to receive feedback and collaborate with othersEagerness to learn and contribute in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment How to ApplyReady to apply? Complete the general Cultivate Internship application on the Cultivate website. You will not see this specific position listed separately, the general application is used for all Cultivate internship opportunities. During the application process, you’ll be able to indicate your areas of interest.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Mars KIND Finance Internship at Mars, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Mars, Inc. Expires: 09/19/2026 At Mars, we work together to build a better world for people, pets, and the planet. From being a socially responsible business, to investing in our Associates, we're always looking at how we can make tomorrow brighter. As an Associate, you are empowered with the freedom and tools to be yourself, to forge your own path, to build relationships across our global community, to discover the right opportunities for you to grow – all with ample support. Here, you have our ongoing commitment to your growth and development as you work across our world-famous brands. Start your journey at Mars today! Mars KIND Finance Internship Experience As a KIND Finance Intern, you will gain exposure to the following areas: Help our finance teams drive our digital agenda by unlocking analytics capabilities, processes and helping to mold the usage and adoption of next generation applications and technologies Collaborate with various stakeholders to drive value through tangible, project-based assignments (vary depending on business need) with visibility to senior leadership within the organization Build capability in sought after skills including but not limited to data storytelling, analysis, process optimization, senior leader communication, project ownership and stakeholder alignment A competitive experience with the potential to join full-time within the MARS Finance Leadership Experience (MFLE) program post-graduation after a successful internship and candidate evaluation. What we’re looking for: We are looking for agile students who have a drive for results, a desire to learn, and who can quickly build relationships We are looking for students who are passionate about the consumer products industry and are majoring in Finance, Accounting, or related business fields Eligible candidates will intern the summer prior to their final graduation date (typically rising seniors) Willingness to relocate to the site of the role Open to students legally authorized to work in the U.S., without the need for current or future work sponsorship Employment is contingent upon successful completion of drug & background screening Eligible candidates will be responsible for personal transportation to and from work site during duration of the internship program. What can you expect from Mars? The Mars Internship Experience is a 10-week summer program providing excellent depth of experience with real business problems and opportunities. Exciting professional and social engagement activities throughout the experience that provide opportunities to network with your intern peers all the way up to senior leaders. Best-in-class training and development from Day 1, including a formal mentor, access to our in-house Mars University, and more. Ongoing coaching and mentorship to help you succeed and get the most out of your experience. Some pretty sweet perks including competitive salary & benefits package, fun freebies, and pet-friendly offices. About Mars, Incorporated For more than a century, Mars, Incorporated has been driven by the belief that the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. This idea is at the center of who we have always been as a global, family-owned business. Today, Mars is transforming, innovating, and evolving in ways that affirm our commitment to making a positive impact on the world around us. Across our diverse and expanding portfolio of Snacking, Food, and Petcare products and services, we employ over 140,000 dedicated Associates who are all moving in the same direction: forward. As a $65 billion family-owned business, we produce some of the world’s best-loved brands including ROYAL CANIN®, PEDIGREE®, WHISKAS®, CESAR®, M&M’S®, SNICKERS®, Pringles®, Cheez-It®, and BEN’S ORIGINAL™. and take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health and services businesses, including AniCura, Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, and VCA™. We know we can only be truly successful if our partners and the communities in which we operate prosper as well. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire our Associates to take action every day to help create a world tomorrow in which the planet, its people and pets can thrive. The Mars Compass, inspired by the Economics of Mutuality, is used to measure the company’s progress in service of its purpose; The world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. For more information about Mars, please visit mars.com. Join us on Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube.

jobs.title: Engineering Intern at Polaris Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 09/19/2026 Internship Program Overview The Polaris Engineering Internship is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. This program is for future leaders who seek a culture built on innovation, passion, and collaboration. As an Engineering Intern, you will be given impactful, project-based assignments that allow you to have exposure to multiple facets of engineering so you will experience both larger ongoing projects as well as shorter-scale projects throughout the summer that align with our business objectives. You will be placed into a specific team based on interest and business needs. These teams could include, but are not limited to: Design Engineering Project Engineering Systems Engineering Test or Development Engineering Potential Placement Locations Could Include: Roseau, MN; Wyoming, MN; Huntsville, AL; or San Angelo, TX, Novi, MI As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services, your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to and from the office. Required Qualifications: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master's degree in Engineering (e.g. mechanical, electrical, computer, software, or systems engineering) with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Able to complete full 12-week internship working 40 hours per week within the dates: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework Previous Internship/Co-op experience Previous experience using CAD or equivalent software (Creo highly desired) Hands-on engineering experience through prior internship or clubs (ex. SAE, Clean Snow) This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

jobs.description: Employer: POSH Cars Expires: 09/19/2026 About POSHPOSH is a luxury vehicle subscription company built on a simple idea: people should be able to access premium vehicles without the long-term commitment, depreciation risk, or paperwork of ownership or a traditional lease. Managing both sides of this, the customer relationship and the fleet partner relationship, is what keeps POSH running.We're a small, fast-moving team, which means interns here get real responsibility, not busywork.About the RolePOSH is hiring an Account Manager Intern for fall 2026 with potential extension based on performance and business needs. This role sits at the intersection of customer success and fleet partner management.Once a customer signs on with POSH, this person becomes their main point of contact. They'll manage the relationship through the life of the subscription, handle questions and issues, and make sure the customer has a good experience that leads to retention.On the other side, this person will also manage relationships with our Fleet Partners. Fleet Partners are the backbone of our fleet, and keeping them informed, satisfied, and issue-free is critical to our supply chain.This is not a shadowing role. The intern will own a portfolio of accounts and partners and be expected to run point on them independently, with support from the team.What You'll Be Responsible ForActing as the main point of contact for customers after the sale, through onboarding, active subscription, renewals, and any issues that come upOwning customer success metrics, including satisfaction, retention, payments and timely resolution of complaintsManaging day-to-day communication with Fleet Partners, including status updates, issue resolution, and answering questions about vehicle performance or paymentsMaintaining accurate and organized records of every account and partner interactionBuilding recurring reports on account health, customer status, and partner activity for leadership reviewSpotting patterns, whether it's a customer segment showing early churn signs or a partner with recurring vehicle issues, and escalating them before they become bigger problemsWorking cross-functionally with Sales, Operations, Billing, and Fleet teams to resolve issues that touch more than one departmentSupporting process improvements for how customer and partner accounts are tracked and managedHelping maintain dashboards or reporting tools that track key account and partner metricsWhat We're Looking ForCurrently pursuing an undergraduate degree, any majorPrior experience in sales, account management, customer success, or a similar client-facing role is preferredExcellent written and verbal communication, this role is customer-facing and requires professionalismStrong analytical skills and comfort working with data to identify trends and inform decisionsHigh attention to detail. Small errors in account records or reporting can have real downstream consequencesA strong sense of ownership. This is not a role where you wait to be told what to doProficiency in Excel, including comfort with formulas and organizing data. Experience with dashboards or reporting tools is a plusStrong time management and the ability to juggle multiple accounts and partners at onceA proactive, problem-solving mindsetComfortable working in a fast-paced, small-team environment where responsibilities can shiftWhat You'll GainDirect ownership over real customer and partner relationships from your first weeks, not simulated projectsExposure to both sides of the business, sales-adjacent customer success and operational fleet partner managementHands-on experience with reporting and data management that informs real business decisionsClose mentorship from a lean team where your work is visible and has direct impactA strong foundation for a career in account management, customer success, or operations

jobs.description: Employer: County of Orange - County of Orange Expires: 09/19/2026 Position Land Survey Paid Intern (Technical Intern)Deadline to ApplyPlease note the deadline for this recruitment is Wednesday, September 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM (PT). OC Public Works (OCPW) provides services on a regional basis to unincorporated areas, to cities, and to other County agencies and departments. The primary mission of the department is to protect and enrich the community through the sustainable delivery of projects and services. OC Public Works’ guiding principles are safety, integrity, quality, teamwork, and adaptability.OCPW is a unique County department comprised of ten (10) service areas: Administrative Services, Agricultural Commissioner/Sealer of Weights & Measures; OC Construction; OC Development Services; OC Environmental Resources; OC Facilities Design & Construction and CUF; OC Facilities Maintenance; OC Fleet Services; OC Infrastructure Programs; OC Operations & Maintenance.OC CONSTRUCTIONOC Construction provides project management and construction management services for projects on OC Public Works' Capital Improvement Program (CIP) and Maintenance Improvement Program (MIP) as well as OC Parks and other County department projects. OC Construction focuses on horizontal projects such as roads, bridges, bikeways, and flood control channels.For more information on OC Public Works click here.For more information on the County of Orange click here.THE OPPORTUNITYThe Land Survey Intern position provides students with valuable hands-on experience by working alongside licensed land surveyors and experienced professionals on a wide variety of public infrastructure projects throughout Orange County. Interns have the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge in a real-world setting while gaining exposure to both office and field surveying practices. Land Survey Interns will assist survey staff with a variety of office and field assignments.Land Survey Interns will assist survey staff with a variety of office and field assignments, including: Assisting with boundary, topographic, construction, hydrographic, and control surveys. Collecting field measurements using GNSS, total stations, digital levels, terrestrial laser scanners, and UAV technologies. Processing field data and assisting with drafting, mapping, and preparation of survey deliverables using CAD and survey software. Assisting with research of deeds, maps, survey records, right-of-way documents, and other legal records. Organizing project files, field notes, and digital records. Performing other related technical duties that support the Survey-Field Services unit while developing practical knowledge of professional land surveying practices. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSThis recruitment is open to applicants who are currently enrolled in or have graduated within the last six (6) months from an accredited college or university pursuing a degree or certificate in Land Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, or a closely related field. Completion of introductory coursework in mathematics, surveying, engineering, or mapping is desirable. Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations and pay close attention to detail. SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONSThe ideal candidate for this Internship will have basic computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office applications. Interest in learning modern land surveying principles, field procedures, and office workflows; surveying equipment, including GNSS/GPS receivers, total stations, digital levels, laser scanners, and other survey technologies; and survey software, including AutoCAD Civil 3D, Trimble Business Center (TBC), GIS applications, or similar programs. Ability to communicate effectively, follow written and verbal instructions, and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.TIME COMMITMENTThis is an in-person internship. Interns may work 26-30 hours per week for 1 year (part-time) not to exceed 1,040 hours. Hours must be scheduled during normal business hours (Monday - Thursday between 6:00am and 3:30pm & Friday between 6:00am and 2:30pm).BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO THE INTERNInterns are offered an excellent opportunity to:Provides students with valuable hands-on experience working alongside licensed land surveyors and experienced professionals.Offers exposure to a wide variety of public infrastructure projects throughout Orange County.Allows interns to apply classroom knowledge in a real-world setting.Provides exposure to both office and field surveying practices.Helps students develop skills and knowledge relevant to entry-level surveying positions.Provides OC Public Works with a larger candidate pool for the entry-level Surveyor I position.Explore a career in local government.Mentorship from management staff.Network with professionals.Apply knowledge through real life application and best practices in field.APPLICATION PROCEDUREApplicants must attach a cover letter, resume, and unofficial transcripts to their application. The cover letter is an opportunity for students to describe career and academic goals, to elaborate upon personal and academic accomplishments, and to identify what type of internship experience they are seeking. Learn more about what to include in a cover letter HERE.Applications that do not include a cover letter, resume, and unofficial transcripts will not be considered.REQUIRED BACKGROUND SCREENING/REFERENCE CHECKPrior to placement, applicants may be asked to submit contact information for reference checks, and a background screening will be conducted that requires a state issued driver's license or ID card and a U.S. Social Security number.

jobs.title: Program Manager Premier College Intern Program at WPAFB Program Manager Trainee Program
jobs.description: Employer: WPAFB Program Manager Trainee Program Expires: 09/20/2026 About WPAFB Program Manager Trainee ProgramLooking for Civilian Program Managers to lead the Air Force into the 21st centuryOne of six centers under Air Force Materiel Command, the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center is the single center responsible for total life cycle management of Air Force weapon systems.The AFLCMC Mission: "Acquire and Support War-Winning Capabilities"Our Motto: "AFLCMC...Providing the Warfighter's Edge"We are currently recruiting Sophomore or Junior students to come work for the U.S. Air Force at Wright-Patterson AFB as a Program Manager in the Premier College Intern Program for the summer of 2027. What is a Program Manager (PM)? What does a Program Manager do in the Air Force?An Acquisition Program Manager leads a team of multi-functional professionals in the acquisition and support of Air Force weapon systems: aircraft, weapons, training systems, IT and business systems at the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC). As an Air Force program manager you will be responsible for managing and coordinating all aspects of an acquisition program to achieve the cost, schedule, performance and sustainment goals of your customers, the men and women who fly, operate, or maintain this country’s most advanced aircraft and systems. Your primary role will be that of the team leader. You will be "the buck stops here" individual who must be able to solve problems and make decisions by leading and motivating a diverse group of individuals to perform as a cohesive and effective team. The acquisition program manager must have organizational and people skills, communication skills, and analytical skills. Additionally, as the leader of a multi-functional team, the program manager must be familiar with the roles and responsibilities of the other team members (logistics managers, financial managers, engineers and contracting specialists, etc.) Experienced, senior program managers often manage an entire aircraft program, like the F-22 Raptor. But as a new program manager, you will more often be responsible for a piece of a major program, like the modification of an item that is integral to an aircraft. Your responsibilities will grow rapidly as you gain experience and demonstrate the ability to handle more complex acquisition programs.These are full time (40 hour/week) positions at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base for 10 to 12 weeks over the summer of 2027. After successful completion of the PM Summer Intern Program, the individual is offered a full-time PM position to start as a GS-07 upon successful completion of a bachelors degree. Pay is set by number of course hours complete at the start of the internship. If 60 or more course hours, you will be paid at the GS-04 level. If more than 120 course hours complete, you will be paid at the GS-05 level. What we need from you:- If interested in this position please send me your updated resume and transcripts to devon.aey@us.af.mil. After verifying eligibility, I will reach out to you to set up an interview. Questions:- If you have any questions at all, please feel free to contact the USAF POC Devon Aey at devon.aey@us.af.mil. He is ready and willing to address any questions you may have or discuss more about the Job or the Program. Don’t hesitate to email.
